study_identification_part.si4_title: Extreme deviations from the normative model reveal cortical heterogeneity and associations with negative symptom severity in first-episode psychosis from the OPTiMiSE and GAP studies

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To apply normative modelling of cortical thickness to first-episode psychosis (FEP) patients to quantify heterogeneity, assess group-level differences between patients and controls, and evaluate whether patterns of cortical atypicality can predict symptoms and response to antipsychotic medication at timepoints from baseline up to 95 weeks.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Mann-Whitney U tests on z-scores for each brain region comparing FEP patients vs controls, with Benjamini-Hochberg correction for multiple comparisons. Linear mixed-effects models (LME) using lmer/lmerTest and glmer/lme4 in R v4.1.1, with time (weeks) and regional z-score as fixed effects, random intercept and slope for subject and time. Dependent variables: PANSS subscales (negative, positive, general), remission status (binary logistic), and remission score (sum of Andreasen criteria items). Regional overlap calculated as percentage of patients/controls with extreme deviations. Chi-square tests for comparing proportions of extreme deviations between groups. Sensitivity analyses excluding sites with fewer than 10 controls.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: At psychosis onset, FEP patients show widespread, highly heterogeneous cortical thinning (no more than 6.4% regional overlap), and baseline negative deviations in parietal and temporal cortex predict more severe negative symptoms over medium-term follow-up.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: First-episode psychosis patients displayed highly heterogeneous patterns of cortical thickness deviations, with no more than 6.4% of patients showing extreme negative deviations in any single brain region (regions with >5% overlap: bilateral inferior precentral gyrus, left post-ventral cingulate, left paracentral gyrus). FEP patients showed a higher percentage of extreme negative deviations (1.77%) compared to controls (0.77%), while controls showed more extreme positive deviations (0.88% vs 0.59%). Mann-Whitney U tests revealed significantly lower z-scores in FEP patients across frontal, temporal, parietal, and occipital lobes (p < 0.05, FDR-corrected). Linear mixed-effects modeling showed that mean cortical thickness z-score predicted negative PANSS scores over time (p = 0.001, coefficient = -0.154), with 12 specific regions in parietal and temporal lobes remaining significant after multiple comparison correction (including left postcentral gyrus, left inferior parietal gyrus, bilateral superior temporal gyrus). Left central gyral deviations predicted remission status (p = 0.0004, coefficient = 0.415, OR = 1.423). No significant relationships were found between cortical deviations and positive or general PANSS scores.

Some FEP patients were exposed to medications at the time of scanning, thus we cannot exclude any effects that medication might have had on cortical thickness." ... "Our large-scale normative model is built from datasets across Europe where ethnicity data is not always available or is measured in a crude way" ... Also, although highly significant, the effects that we report are of moderate magnitude and we consider that validation in prospective data is an important next step"

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Federated learning approach allows adaptation of pre-trained normative model to new sites without transferring sensitive clinical data. Model adaptation used 50% of local control data to learn site effects while avoiding removal of clinically relevant variance. Z-scores from multiple sites become comparable after harmonization, enabling combination into a single sample for statistical analysis without including site/sex as covariates in later models. Remission status was defined using Schizophrenia Working Group Consensus criteria; a summed remission score was also computed for increased statistical power.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The pre-trained reference normative model was from Kia et al. 2020/2022 (N=37,126, 79 scanners, age 6-100 years). The ATLAS study data was used to supplement GAP controls for older age range representation. Clinical follow-up ranged from 0-95 weeks with median 4 assessments per patient. Both GAP (ICD-10) and OPTiMiSE (DSM-IV) diagnostic criteria were used. The study demonstrated that normative modeling detected remission prediction that was not possible using cortical thickness alone in previous work on the OPTiMiSE sample. Additional sensitivity analyses excluded sites with <10 controls after adaptation. This study represents the first report of cortical thickness with reference to a large multi-site normative model at both group- and individual-level in FEP patients.
